title: Per-usage attribution explorer: billing slices, time-series, and soft-quota previews
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Design and prototype a per-usage attribution explorer inside Redwood Console that lets engineers and finance teams:.
- Inspect token-level cost slices for a given date range and route (per-request breakdown).
- Attribute cost to features, routes, and model variants with adjustable weighting for shared prompts (system vs user tokens).
- Export detailed CSV/Parquet for billing reconciliation and external accounting tools.
- Preview soft-quota and predicted overage cost by extrapolating current usage trends.
Goal: Provide transparent, actionable cost tooling that supports both debugging (why did this job cost X?) and macro-level budgeting (which routes are the biggest drivers of spend).
decisions: Show both absolute token counts and dollar cost side-by-side; cost uses net unit price from pricing config (includes discounts).
Default attribution is 'route-first' with option to toggle 'model-variant-first' and 'session-based' attribution.
Expose two export formats: flattened CSV for finance teams and nested Parquet for analytics pipelines.
Include a 'sample request' detail panel that shows raw tokens (truncated) and which tokens were cached vs generated.
tradeoffs: Token-level detail increases query cost and latency — we will page and sample by default, with an explicit toggle to 'load full detail'.
Retention vs privacy: full token strings are visible in prototype but behind a permission flag and redaction policy in production.
Rounding vs precision: display rounded dollars on hover for clarity, full precision in export to avoid reconciliation drift.
progress_updates: 2025-11-10: Kickoff — aligned with PM (Rodrigo Evans) and Eng (Leila Kaur) on metrics and required backend endpoints (ENG-2401).
2025-11-13: Low-fidelity wireframes completed — focused on three panes: time-series, attribution table, request inspector.
2025-11-15: Hi-fi Figma prototype delivered; tradeoff review with security on token redaction patterns (security review flagged but not blocking).
2025-11-18: Eng review — backend contract updated to include 'attribution_reason' per request and export job endpoint (ENG-2417).
2025-11-21: Design review scheduled with PM and Finance partner; addressing feedback about default row sorting and CSV column ordering.
review_notes: PM (Rodrigo Evans): Add KPI header that surfaces 'Predicted month-end spend' using linear extrapolation and a confidence band.
Eng (Leila Kaur): Backend can provide exact token attribution but queries more expensive; recommend server-side paging and a 'download full export' background job.
Finance (Marta Nguyen): CSV column ordering must match current billing schema: invoice_item, route_id, model, tokens_user, tokens_system, tokens_total, unit_price, total_cost, attribution_tag.
Security (Caleb Ortiz): Sensitive system prompts must be redacted by default; add 'redaction consent' flag for accounts with proper data agreements.
acceptance_criteria: Design mockups (desktop) for time-series, attribution table, request inspector, and export modal exist in Figma and are linked.
Prototype demonstrates paging, sampling toggle, and CSV export flow for both finance and engineering formats.
Design spec includes accessibility checks for table keyboard navigation and color contrast for cost heatmaps.
Edge cases documented: routes with mixed model variants, cached responses attribution, and failed request handling.
next_steps: Incorporate finance CSV ordering feedback and produce final export spec (owner: Marcos).
Work with Eng to define API contract for background export job and soft-quota prediction endpoint (owner: Leila).
Add consent flow copy for token redaction and send to Legal for review (owner: Aisha).
Prepare design QA checklist and handoff package for implementation sprint 2025-W48.
notes: Prototype emphasizes developer workflows (debugging specific costly requests) and finance workflows (monthly reconciliations). We intentionally separate the UI paths but reuse the same export backend. Consider future 'rules' UI to auto-tag attribution based on route regexes.
